Ernest Hemingway as a teenager at the wheel of an American Red Cross ambulance during World War I. Italy. 1918.

Early in 1918, Hemingway responded to a Red Cross recruitment effort and signed on to become an ambulance driver in Italy. He only drove an ambulance for 2 months before he was seriously wounded by mortar fire, having just returned from the canteen bringing chocolate and cigarettes for the men at the front line. Despite his wounds, Hemingway assisted Italian soldiers to safety, for which he received the Italian Silver Medal of Bravery, He underwent an immediate operation at a distribution center, and spent five days at a field hospital before he was transferred for recuperation to the Red Cross hospital in Milan, where he spent six months.

While recuperating, he fell in love, for the first time, with Agnes von Kurowsky, a Red Cross nurse seven years his senior who later inspired the character "Catherine Barkley" in Hemingway's A Farewell to Arms.
